clue.text: Prompt indication of future trends in financial reporting?

definitions.note: a verb here: to stir up or instigate

indicators.note: in places the sign of things to come within the newspaper's initials

parts.note: the FT, the Financial Times, is the UK's financial newspaper
an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: A question about whether business journalism can tell you which way the markets are heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' looks like an adjective meaning quick, but it is a verb, to incite. The FT is the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: To foment trouble is to instigate or stir it up, which is to prompt it.

clue.text: German physicist to succeed bottling hydrogen in the works

indicators.note: bottling means holding the chemical symbol inside like a bottle

parts.note: to fare well is to get on, and fare alone means to manage or succeed
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

indicators.note: works suggests these letters are being worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A German scientist makes his name by bottling gas in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the works' looks like a factory, but 'in the' is the fodder and 'works' rearranges it to NHEIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit was a German-born physicist who devised a temperature scale.

clue.text: "Alien to spoil it after turning up" — a Nationalist

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word it is written bottom to top

explanation.surface: A quoted slogan in which a nationalist tells someone to wreck things.
explanation.definitionFit: A being from the planet Mars is the classic science-fiction extraterrestrial.

clue.text: Honourably turned on by embracing ladies primarily

indicators.note: turned means the short word on is written backwards
embracing means by wraps round the initial
primarily means only the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone is gallantly aroused by hugging women, chiefly.
explanation.definitionFit: To act nobly is to act with honour and high principle.

clue.text: US writer omitting name of apostle in version of Bible

indicators.note: in places the shortened apostle within the Bible version's letters

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version, the King James Bible

indicators.note: omitting means one letter is left out of the apostle's name

parts.note: Simon (Peter) was one of the twelve apostles

explanation.surface: A cut-down Bible translation drops the name of one of the disciples.
explanation.walkthrough: Part of a science-fiction theme with Bradbury, Foundation and Fahrenheit elsewhere in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was the American science-fiction author of the Foundation novels.

clue.text: Notice European harbour feature accommodating 100 — that's competence

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

indicators.note: accommodating means the harbour structure has the numeral inside it

parts.note: a quay is a landing place in a harbour
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: An announcement says a European dock can take a hundred, proving its capability.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequacy means being sufficient or capable enough for a task, as competence does.

clue.text: Place having additional numbers around after I beg

indicators.note: after means the rest is written following the opening pronoun
around means the larger quantity wraps round the place abbreviation

parts.note: more means additional in number
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A venue with extra seats is wanted, and someone pleads for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I beg' sounds like the speaker's plea; 'I' is wordplay and 'beg' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to plead or entreat earnestly, as when begging.

clue.text: Males losing head are contributors to rows

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: boars are male pigs

explanation.surface: Men lose their tempers and stir up quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' reads as arguments; it is rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing a boat is done with paddles worked by the crew, so these are what make rowing happen.

clue.text: Very sweet woman's engaged in applying the third degree?

indicators.note: engaged in means the female pronoun is held inside the other piece

parts.note: cubic means raised to the third power, a punning reading of the third degree
read as 'woman is', the woman giving her

explanation.surface: An angelic-looking woman is caught up in a harsh police interrogation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The third degree' suggests rough questioning, but here it is the mathematical third power, cubing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubic means like a cherub, innocently and angelically sweet-faced.

clue.text: Times of commemoration seen with certain parties

indicators.note: parties, as a verb meaning celebrates wildly, suggests the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Anniversaries are spotted alongside particular political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Hundredth anniversaries are occasions for commemorating events of a century ago.

clue.text: European country keeping parliamentarian in government

definitions.note: here a noun for rule or dominion

indicators.note: keeping means the country holds the politician inside it

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A European nation has an MP serving in its ruling administration.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a realm under one supreme authority, so the word can mean sovereign rule.

clue.text: Variable administrators of chess taking step back to improve

indicators.note: stepping back means the chess body's initials are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: FIDE is the World Chess Federation, the game's governing body
Y is a typical algebraic variable

explanation.surface: The fickle officials who run chess retreat on a move in order to do better.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to instruct someone so as to improve them morally or intellectually.

clue.text: One transmits notes about currency

indicators.note: about means the two notes surround the currency

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for note, so two notes give two Ns
the euro is the European currency

explanation.surface: A broadcaster passes on banknotes relating to the money supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One transmits' sounds like a radio station; it is a nerve cell passing on impulses.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve cell carries electrical impulses through the nervous system, so it transmits signals.

clue.text: Start at one, working to produce primer

parts.note: to found something is to start it
I is the Roman numeral for one
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Beginning at the first step and working up to make a basic reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primer' suggests a schoolbook; it is an undercoat of paint or make-up base.
explanation.definitionFit: A base coat applied before paint or make-up, which prepares the surface, is a primer.

clue.text: Friend in America goes to church

indicators.note: goes to means the following letters attach after the church abbreviation

explanation.surface: A pal in the United States heads off to a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friend in America' looks like the definition, but 'in' and 'America' are wordplay. China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, a London expression.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang china plate rhymes with mate, so a china is a pal.

clue.text: Bird riding big horse

parts.note: a percher is a perching bird, one that sits on branches
riding a horse is being on it

explanation.surface: A bird sits perched on the back of a large horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' seems to want a specific species; it is the general term for a perching bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The Percheron is a heavy French draught breed, among the biggest of horses.

clue.text: US writer, poet with change of heart, to get engrossed

indicators.note: a change of heart means the middle letters swap places

parts.note: a bard is a poet
to bury oneself in something is to become engrossed

explanation.surface: A poet's change of mind leaves an American author absorbed in his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Ray Bradbury was the American science-fiction author of Fahrenheit 451.

clue.text: Book expert, one under one zodiacal sign not initially following another

indicators.note: following means the trimmed person comes after the other star sign

parts.note: Libra is another sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is removed

parts.note: an Arian is someone born under Aries

explanation.surface: A bookish type is described in horoscope terms, born under one sign and then another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One under one zodiacal sign' is a person born under Aries, an Arian; it loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A librarian looks after a collection of books and knows their way around them.

clue.text: Pragmatic approach is adopted by field of study

indicators.note: adopted by means the short word is taken inside the other piece

parts.note: a realm is a domain or sphere of study

explanation.surface: A practical method is taken up by an academic discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism means accepting things as they are and dealing with them practically.

clue.text: A weight, carrying coals to Newcastle? On the contrary

indicators.note: carrying means the letters sit inside the phrase that follows
on the contrary flips the saying: the words coals to Newcastle carry the weight, not the other way round

explanation.surface: Taking coal to Newcastle is the proverbial pointless delivery; here the clue jokes that the phrase itself carries the load.
explanation.walkthrough: Newcastle was England's great coal port, so carrying coals there is a byword for a needless act.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone is an imperial unit of weight of fourteen pounds, still used in Britain for body weight.

clue.text: Corporation anger reduced after introduction of British vehicle

indicators.note: after means the cut-down anger comes following that letter

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a pot belly, and tum is a belly

indicators.note: introduction of means only the opening letter of the next word
reduced means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to rile is to anger

explanation.surface: A city council's fury is calmed once a British carriage arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' reads as a company or council; it is a jocular word for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbril is a cart, famously used to take prisoners to the guillotine in the French Revolution.

clue.text: Limits to growth set by one Indian leader

indicators.note: set by means the numeral is placed beside the letters before it

parts.note: the limits of the word growth are its end letters, G and H, written out with the linking word
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The Limits to Growth is a famous report on economic expansion, here credited to a leader in India.
explanation.walkthrough: The limits to 'growth' are 'G and H' read literally, conjunction included.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence movement against British rule.

clue.text: Drink provided by drink provider runs short? It requires steps to be taken

definitions.text: It requires steps to be taken

parts.note: rum is a spirit

indicators.note: short means the pub is lacking the runs abbreviation

parts.note: a bar serves drinks
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A bar runs out of rum, and you are told to take steps about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It requires steps to be taken' sounds like a remedy for a problem; the steps are dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance, performed in a set pattern of steps.

clue.text: Billion invested in basic automatic device

indicators.note: invested in means the abbreviation is placed inside the other word

parts.note: root, as in root cause, means basic or fundamental

explanation.surface: A billion is put into a basic machine that runs itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that carries out tasks on its own programming is a mechanical automaton.

clue.text: Drink popular between bridge partners

indicators.note: between means the popular word sits in the middle of the two partners

parts.note: West and East are partners at the bridge table
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A drink goes down well between partners at the card table.
explanation.definitionFit: A fermented grape beverage, red or white, served with a meal.

clue.text: The writer's turned round story associated with university environment

indicators.note: turned round means the contraction for the writer is reversed

parts.note: the writer is the setter, 'I am', contracted to I'm
a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: An author changes their account after a tale about campus life.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is a person's social setting or surroundings.

clue.text: Recalled difficulty entering top-rated British and American city areas

indicators.note: recalled means the whole assembled string is called back, read in reverse
entering means the difficulty goes inside the other letters

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI
a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A troublesome problem resurfaces in the best-rated British and American cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reverses everything once RUB has been put inside AIBUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Suburbia is the collective term for the outer residential districts of cities.

clue.text: Appropriate picture — source of light in heavens

parts.note: to picture something is to see it in the mind

indicators.note: in places the initial letter inside the exclamation

parts.note: 'Heavens!' and 'My!' are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: source of means just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A painting showing the origin of light in the sky fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemly means fitting or in keeping with good taste, so proper or suitable.

clue.text: Hot line seen in various notes

indicators.note: seen in means the line letter appears inside the rearranged letters
various suggests the letters of notes in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A sizzling melody can be heard across a range of musical notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges NOTES to STOEN for the L to sit in.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for stolen goods, ones too recently taken to sell safely.
